<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par90 />Rem. The above examples are mostly rendered definite by the article, or by a following genitive of definition, or are proper names. But cases like {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫מָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫יְתָה}} show that the locative form ''of itself'' possessed a defining power.

{{GHGmargin-letter|90|d}}
(''b'') In a somewhat weakened sense, indicating the place ''where'' something is or happens (cf. {{GHGpar|118|d}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲנָ֑יְמָה|translate=in Maḥanaim}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=4|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה|translate=there}} (usually ''thither'', see c), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=2}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=8}}, and the expression ''to offer a sacrifice'' {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבֵּ֫חָה}}, properly ''towards the altar'' for ''on the altar''. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=בָּבֶ֫לָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=15}}, and {{GHGheb|text=זְבֻ֫לָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=11}}, are to be regarded as ordinary accusatives of direction, ''to Babylon, into the habitation''; also expressions like {{GHGheb|text=פְּאַת צָפ֫וֹנָה|translate=the quarter towards the north}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=5}} (at the beginning of the verse, {{GHGheb|text=גְּבוּל קֵ֫דְמָה|translate=the border toward the east}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=15.20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|90|e}}
(''c'') The original force of the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is also disregarded when it is added to a substantive with a preposition prefixed (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אָ֫נָה|translate=how long?}}), and this not only after {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} or {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}} (which are easily explained), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עְלָה|translate=upwards}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫טָּה|translate=downwards}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁא֫וֹלָה|translate=to Sheol}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אֲפֵ֫קָה|translate=unto Aphek}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=13|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־הַצָּפ֫וֹנָה|translate=toward the north}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=16}}; but also after {{GHGheb|text=ב}}, and even after {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּנֶּ֫גְבָּה|translate=in the south}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=21}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=15.19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=31|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=52|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִבָּבֶ֫לָה|translate=from Babylon}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=16}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=6}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|90|f}}
Rem. Old locative forms (or original accusatives) are, according to the Masora, still to be found in

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יְלָה}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫יְלָה}}, the usual word in prose for ''night'', which is always construed as masculine. The nominative of this supposed old accusative<ref>Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Sem. Sprachwiss}}., p. 113, also takes it as such, ''láylā'' being properly ''at night'', then ''night'' simply. Barth, however (''Sprachwiss. Abhandlungen'', p. 16, note 1), refers it to an original {{GHGheb|text=לַיְלֶה}}, like {{GHGheb|text=אָנָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָנֶ֫ה}}.</ref> appeared to be preserved in the form {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יִל}}, only used in poetry, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=3}}, ''constr. st''. {{GHGheb|text=לֵיל}} (even used for the ''absol. st''. in pause {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=11}}). Most probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=לַיְלָה}} is to be referred, with Nöldeke and others, to a reduplicated form {{GHGheb|text=לילי}}; cf. especially the western Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=לֵילְיָא}}, Syr. ''lilya'', &c.—Another instance is {{GHGheb|text=מְא֫וּמָה|translate=something}}, probably from {{GHGheb|text=מְאוּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוּם|translate=spot, point}}, generally with a negative=''nothing''. Similarly {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫רְצָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=23}} and (in pause) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=13}}, {{GHGheb|text=סוּפָ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=7}}, and the place-name {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫הְצָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=6|verse=63}}, might be explained as accusatives. Elsewhere, however, the toneless {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} can be regarded only as a meaningless appendage, or at the most as expressing poetic emphasis; thus {{GHGheb|text=אָ֫רְצָה}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַמָּ֫וְתָה|translate=death}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֶגְדָּה־נָּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=14.18}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫חְלָה|translate=stream}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=124|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַחַשְׁמַ֫לָה|translate=amber}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=2}} [in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=4|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַחַשְׁמַל}}, cf. {{GHGpar|80|k}}], &c. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הַיָּ֫מָּה}} is probably only a scribal error (dittography). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=18}} instead of the quite unsuitable poetic word {{GHGheb|text=הַחַ֫רְסָה}} (towards the sun??) read as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=1|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַחַ֫דְרָה|translate=to the bride-chamber}}.
